Hi Susan — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a couple of asks from procurement/ops so we can land an onboarding path: 

- Procurement readiness: Do you anticipate onboarding Redwood via a Purchase Order (PO) or corporate card/virtual card?
- Marketplace: you mentioned finance sometimes prefers marketplace provisioning for smaller vendors — is AWS Marketplace (or similar) something Procurement would consider to speed this up?
- Docs: If PO, can you confirm which vendor forms (W9, vendor setup doc, SOC2) Procurement will require up front?

Next steps I propose:
1) If PO path: we email your procurement contact the vendor onboarding form and a statement of work (SOW) draft — typical turnaround 7–10 business days.
2) If card/virtual card: we can enable subscription billing and invoice afterward; we’ll need a billing contact and PO number (if you use it on the invoice).
3) If marketplace: I’ll check marketplace SKUs and share the onboarding link.

Attaching a blank vendor onboarding form in my follow-up (Marissa will share). If you can loop in your AP/procurement contact (or forward this thread) that will speed decisions.

Hi Susan / HelioMed procurement — I’m Marissa from Commercial Ops, picking this up to outline options and what each path requires. Attached: vendor_onboarding_form.xlsx (fillable).

Short summary:
- PO route (recommended for multi-quarter engagements):
  * Required: completed vendor onboarding form, W9 (US), SOC2 Type II or equivalent evidence, signed quote/SOW.
  * Timeline: once we receive completed forms and a PO, vendor setup typically takes 5–8 business days; contract signature adds depending on your legal queue.
  * Billing: monthly or net-30 invoices tied to PO number. We can invoice multiple cost centers (please specify account codes on the PO).

- Virtual/corporate card (fastest for pilots <$50k):
  * Required: billing contact + card details/virtual card.
  * Timeline: immediate subscription activation; monthly statement/invoice after the fact.

- Marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure):
  * Pros: faster procurement, reduced paperwork for the buyer; cons: marketplace fees and possible SKU limitations. We can publish a marketplace listing if HelioMed wants to go that route — I’ll flag product to confirm SKUs and pricing parity.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) HelioMed confirms preferred path (PO / card / marketplace) and provides procurement contact (name + email).
2) We send completed onboarding form + SOC2 attestation + draft SOW (attached as link in my follow-up).
3) If PO: HelioMed issues PO — we begin vendor setup and schedule an onboarding kickoff.

Karthik — can you confirm any AP constraints we should be aware of (PO number formats, vendor payment terms exceptions)?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Marissa / Logan — I’m Tom from HelioMed Procurement (forwarded from procurement@heliomed.com). A few constraints and answers from our side: 

- We require vendor tax forms (W9), vendor setup questionnaire, and a SOC2 summary. We can accept a SOC2 letter or an audit report — redacted version is fine.
- For contracts: PO is our default for any spend > $50k annually. We will accept virtual cards for pilots under that threshold, but vendor onboarding still requires completed supplier info (matrix attached).
- Marketplace: We prefer marketplace for smaller vendors to speed time-to-live, but only if the pricing is equivalent. If Redwood can provide a marketplace SKU for the pilot we’d prefer that.
- Invoicing: we can invoice to multiple cost centers if the PO includes the cost-center splits, but that requires your invoices to include cost-center lines.

I’ve attached our supplier matrix and procurement_policy.pdf for your intake team to confirm. Please send: completed onboarding form + SOC2 attestation + draft SOW/quote. If you support DocuSign for signature, send the envelope link and I’ll route to Legal.

Regards,
Tom Breen
Procurement Manager, HelioMed
t.breen@heliomed.com
